subject: obstetrics-gynaecology
title: Artery Ligation, Retained Placenta, Inversion and Amniotic Embolism

steps.tx: Tying the ascending uterine artery at the lower segment devascularises the uterus stepwise as **uterine artery ligation**. Adding tubo ovarian anastomosis ligation completes the stepwise devascularisation ladder. Fertility and menstruation usually survive the procedure. Careful history taking and examination help place this finding in the right clinical context before treatment is planned.
steps.say: Uterine artery ligation stepwise devascularises the uterus while preserving fertility usually.

steps.tx: Ligating the anterior division of the internal iliac artery reduces pelvic pulse pressure in **internal iliac ligation**. Collaterals prevent tissue necrosis while clotting catches up. It demands retroperitoneal skill and ureter identification. Correlating this finding with imaging and laboratory results prevents both delayed treatment and unnecessary intervention in most patients.
steps.say: Internal iliac ligation reduces pelvic pulse pressure while collaterals prevent necrosis.

steps.tx: Placenta failing to deliver beyond thirty minutes with ongoing management is **retained placenta**. Manual removal under anaesthesia follows, with accreta the feared finding. Prophylactic antibiotics cover the intrauterine manipulation. Early recognition matters because timely treatment gives clearly better outcomes than waiting for complications to develop first.
steps.say: Retained placenta needs manual removal under anaesthesia with accreta feared.

steps.tx: The uterus turning inside out through the cervix, usually from cord traction on an unseparated placenta, is **uterine inversion**. A vaginal mass with absent fundus and shock out of proportion announces it. Immediate manual replacement under relaxation, the Johnson manoeuvre, precedes any placental removal.
steps.say: Uterine inversion turns the uterus inside out and needs immediate manual replacement.

steps.tx: Fetal debris entering maternal circulation causing collapse, seizures and DIC is **amniotic fluid embolism**. Now called anaphylactoid syndrome of pregnancy, it strikes during labour or just after delivery. Supportive critical care is the only treatment. Documenting this finding clearly in the notes guides the next clinician and supports safe, well planned further management.
steps.say: Amniotic fluid embolism collapses the mother with seizures and DIC needing critical care.

steps.tx: Interventional radiology embolising pelvic arteries controls bleeding without laparotomy as **arterial embolisation**. It suits stable patients in equipped centres, often after caesarean haemorrhage. Fertility preservation is its great attraction. When this picture is seen in practice, urgent senior review is wise whenever there is any doubt about severity.
steps.say: Arterial embolisation controls bleeding without laparotomy in stable equipped patients.

steps.tx: Hysterectomy decisions made earlier save lives, following the principle of **timely hysterectomy**. Subtotal hysterectomy is faster when the cervix is not the bleeding source. Pride and fertility hopes must not postpone it past survivability. Understanding this mechanism explains the symptoms, the investigation findings and the logic behind each step of treatment given.
steps.say: Timely hysterectomy saves lives and subtotal operation is faster when suitable.

steps.tx: Secondary haemorrhage days to weeks after delivery usually means infection with retained tissue, termed **secondary PPH**. Ultrasound, antibiotics and gentle evacuation treat it. Ergometrine has a specific role here unlike in primary atony protocols. This distinction changes management, so it should be settled early rather than after empirical treatment has already begun.
steps.say: Secondary PPH days later means infection with retained tissue needing evacuation.

steps.tx: Blood product ratios approximating whole blood guide massive transfusion as **balanced transfusion**. Red cells, plasma and platelets run together with fibrinogen and calcium. Point of care viscoelastic tests refine the recipe. Careful history taking and examination help place this finding in the right clinical context before treatment is planned.
steps.say: Balanced transfusion runs cells, plasma, platelets and fibrinogen together.
